text:
vivian: quick RFC follow-up — we need to pick a default pattern for private customers: regional peering with per-region egress IPs (each region advertises customer routes) vs a shared, centralized egress gateway per-account. pros/cons and cost anchoring ideas?

alex: Regional peering pros: lower latency, simpler path (no extra hop). cons: more IPs to manage per customer, increased peering churn and route scale.

mike: Shared egress gateway pros: single place for auditing/KMS and predictable ip allocation. cons: extra hop adds ~8-15ms, potential throughput bottleneck + single point to scale.

kristin: control-plane implications: regional peering means control-plane only needs to approve peering attachments and push route ACLs. shared gateway requires an additional lifecycle API (create/attach/detach gateway) and new TLS handoff semantics.

alex: also operationally: per-region approach complicates cost attribution. we either bill per-region egress or we "anchor" costs to the customer's account and surface a per-region breakdown in billing.

vivian: on cost anchoring — two options: (A) treat egress as a first-class metered item (per-GB per-region) and pass-through to the customer's billing; (B) pool egress into our infra costs and allocate flat surcharge by SLA tier. thoughts?

mike: prefer A for transparency. customers with predictable traffic want direct visibility. also simplifies chargeback for multi-region customers.

kristin: agree on transparency but warning: per-GB metering + 100s of small customers => billing complexity. need aggregation windows and sampling.

vivian: perf/failover question — if regional peering suffers capacity issues, can we fail traffic to shared gateway? how painful is cross-model fallback?

alex: fallback is doable but requires route precedence and automatic SRV-like ranking. simple approach: maintain a lower-priority route that sends to shared egress NLB. On peering healthy = local, on failure = fallback.

mike: note: we must preserve source IP semantics for some customers. NAT behaviour between models differs. need a compatibility shim.

kristin: shim idea: small sidecar on shared-egress that can SNAT to per-customer IP pools, preserving expected egress IPs when required. adds complexity but helps compatibility.

vivian: quick pseudo-terraform for fallback routing (for the ops doc):
```
resource "aws_route" "to_shared_egress" {
  route_table_id         = var.rt_id
  destination_cidr_block = var.customer_prefix
  # lower priority route via NLB (only used if more specific peering route gone)
  nat_gateway_id         = aws_nat_gateway.shared_egress.id
}
```

alex: ops/limits: ENI quotas per account are the hard limit for regional peering scale. for customers >X vCPU we prefer shared egress to avoid ENI explosion. we should codify thresholds.

vivian: proposal summary:
- default: regional peering for low-to-medium customers (better perf, simpler path)
- fallback: shared egress gateway (automatic route precedence failover)
- billing: default to option A (per-GB per-region) with an aggregation window + invoice spike alerting
- compatibility: sidecar SNAT shim for IP-preservation cases
- threshold: >N ENIs or >Y concurrent flows -> recommend shared egress

kristin: sounds good. action items?

vivian: action items:
- alex: write playbook for route precedence + automated failover (due EOD Fri)
- mike: prototype sidecar SNAT shim and perf test (P0 spike?) (due 2 weeks)
- product: draft billing UI mockup for per-region egress breakdown (ask finance)

infra-bot: automated note — peering metrics for customer "acme-inc" show 95th p95 egress 120Mbps in us-west-2 (from last hour) :bar_chart:

alex: ack, will include test cases for route flap scenarios.

mike: ack, will start load harness.

vivian: thanks everyone. we'll capture this in the RFC follow-up doc and schedule a short sync if needed. :thumbsup:
